The paper studies electromagnetic invisibility cloaks obtained by point transformations from general anisotropic media.
Multiple cloaks located at different points in space are considered.
Tangential components of electric and magnetic fields vanish at the outside boundary ∂K+ of the cloaked object.
Normal components of the curl of electric and magnetic fields vanish at the inside boundary ∂K−.
These boundary conditions are derived by requiring energy conservation.
Permittivity and permeability inside the cloaked object are assumed bounded and with positive lower bounds.
The cloaked object K is surrounded by a cloaking layer defined by a spherical shell.
The transformation blows up a point into a spherical shell, mapping the punctured ball onto the shell.
The Maxwell operator in the cloaking domain has only one self-adjoint extension outside K, ensuring unique energy-preserving dynamics.
Inside and outside solutions are decoupled and generally discontinuous at ∂K.
Self-adjoint boundary conditions correspond to physically meaningful solutions conserving energy.
The paper proves cloaking holds for active devices, including those with currents at the boundary of K.
Approximate cloaks can be improved by adding a lining that enforces the exact cloaking boundary conditions.
The media are assumed non-dispersive, focusing on narrow frequency bands.
The permittivity and permeability tensors are degenerate at the cloaking boundary, causing singular behavior.
The paper uses Schrödinger form of Maxwell equations to analyze boundary conditions.
The transformation media are constructed via bijections that are twice continuously differentiable except possibly at outer boundary spheres.
The cloaking boundary conditions at ∂K+ are always satisfied naturally by the solutions.
The paper generalizes previous results for spherical and cylindrical cloaks to general anisotropic media.
The study includes explicit verification for a spherical cloak with a radial current at the boundary.
The cloaking boundary conditions allow a complete formulation of cloaking as a boundary value problem.
The paper's results apply to cloaking objects inside general crystals with anisotropic properties.
Transmission conditions linking inside and outside solutions are not self-adjoint and thus not physically allowed.
The operator generating the Maxwell dynamics is unitarily equivalent to the free Maxwell propagator outside the cloaked region.
